sources.name: Standard Ebooks
sources.notes: Edited reading editions; individual story links, rather than collection landing pages. Some editions use Gutenberg transcriptions; this is a distinct reading host, not a claim of independent digitization.
sources.focus: Carefully edited classics by Chekhov, Joyce, and Fitzgerald.

sources.name: Wikisource
sources.notes: Community transcriptions, often backed by scans. Host rights statements are jurisdiction-specific; QwikLit links outward without claiming worldwide public-domain clearance.
sources.focus: Classic fiction and early science fiction, with editions from around the world.

sources.name: Lit2Go · University of South Florida
sources.notes: University reading pages with optional audio, word counts, and edition citations. Collection edition year is not asserted as the first publication year.
sources.focus: Classic stories to read or listen to, from the University of South Florida.

sources.name: Library of America · Story of the Week
sources.notes: Publisher selections with introductions and free story PDFs reached from each selection page. New weekly selections can include essays, so automatic indiscriminate import is intentionally avoided.
sources.focus: Rediscovered American writing selected by the Library of America.

sources.name: Edgar Allan Poe Society of Baltimore
sources.notes: Scholarly reading texts with textual and edition history.
sources.focus: Gothic tales and horror from Edgar Allan Poe.

sources.name: George Eliot Archive
sources.notes: Scholarly archive with free digitized editions. Longer works are labeled novella; page gives access to a reading viewer.
sources.focus: George Eliot’s shorter fiction and novellas in early editions.

sources.name: Kate Chopin International Society
sources.notes: Scholarly society, free accurate texts and PDFs; direct reading links are used instead of critical summaries.
sources.focus: Stories of freedom, identity, and everyday life by Kate Chopin.

sources.name: East of the Web
sources.notes: Free classic and contemporary story pages. Fiction-index discovery adds named stories after title/byline verification; dates stay absent when the publisher does not supply them.
sources.focus: Classic stories alongside free fiction by contemporary writers.

sources.name: Peter Watts · Author’s Backlist
sources.notes: Free stories linked by the author, with a Creative Commons notice on the backlist. QwikLit uses metadata-only outbound links; the license is not treated as permission to republish here.
sources.focus: Science fiction shared by the author, from first contact to distant futures.

sources.name: Documenting the American South · UNC
sources.notes: University digitized editions; story anchors point inside the original collection.
sources.focus: Charles W. Chesnutt’s fiction in the University of North Carolina’s literary collection.

sources.name: Mark Twain in His Times · University of Virginia
sources.notes: University scholarly archive with early published story texts.
sources.focus: Mark Twain’s humor and early stories from the University of Virginia.

sources.name: Lightspeed · Free Reprints
sources.notes: Publisher-hosted free fiction. Curated older works, with original publication years separate from the reprint dates.
sources.focus: Free science fiction reprints by Peter Watts and Ken Liu.
